The story

Founded in 1860 by Edouard Heuer in St-Imier, Switzerland, the company quickly established a reputation for precision chronographs. Key innovations include the oscillating pinion in 1887, a component still used in modern chronographs, and the "Mikrograph" in 1916, the first stopwatch accurate to 1/100th of a second. The brand's connection to motorsports began early and was solidified with iconic models like the Monaco, which was introduced in 1969 and featured the first automatic chronograph movement, the Calibre 11. The 1980s brought significant changes, including the introduction of the 2000 series in 1982, a versatile dive watch collection that would later evolve into the popular Aquaracer line. In 1985, the TAG (Techniques d'Avant Garde) Group acquired Heuer, leading to the formation of the TAG Heuer brand as it is known today. This new era saw the launch of the colorful and successful Formula 1 collection in 1986, which was initially a quartz-powered series aimed at a younger audience. The 2000 series also continued to evolve, with models like the 2000 Automatic Chronograph and the later 2000 Exclusive. In 1999, the French luxury goods conglomerate LVMH (Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton) acquired TAG Heuer, further solidifying its position in the luxury market. The brand has continued to push the boundaries of watchmaking with high-concept pieces like the Mikrogirder, which is capable of measuring time with extreme precision. Today, TAG Heuer continues to build on its heritage with modern interpretations of its iconic lines, including various Monaco models like the Monaco 24 Calibre 36 Chronograph and other specific references such as the CAW2116, alongside the ever-popular Aquaracer and Formula 1 collections.
